findings.location: ID-R04, ID-I05, ID-S03 and Unresolved Dependencies item 2; compare contracts/native-codegraph-boundary.md Trusted input and research.md Decision 4
findings.affected_requirement: FR-010 trusted contained tool-state write footprint and Story 18.2 lease ownership
findings.evidence: The plan describes the pending 18.2 adjustment as allowing writes to `.codegraph/**`, but ID-I05/S03 require the trusted coordinator to create the `.codegraph` directory entry first. A descendant-only footprint does not unambiguously authorize creation of that entry. The plan also denies workspace-root creation to the CodeGraph child. Research and the contract repeat pre-creation under the same adjustment without defining the exact entry-creation authority or an owner-provisioned alternative. Pinned CodeGraph init then writes inside the directory, so this ambiguity affects whether the proposed startup can be authorized and executed within the declared footprint.
findings.correction_outcome: Specify the exact 18.2 owner-issued capability for creating the single `.codegraph` directory entry and writing descendants, or require the shared workspace owner to pre-provision and verify that entry before issuing a descendant-only lease. Keep workspace-root creation denied to CLI/MCP children and all other root writes prohibited. Align the plan, contract, research and verification checks without inventing the pending 18.2 interface.

raw_result.summary: PR-18-3-01 remains resolved. The conditional source-copy plan accepted in plan-review-04 is superseded by the user's in-place dedicated-workspace decision; prior definition-review-01 is invalidated. The current plan correctly separates retained source from disposable in-project CodeGraph state, holds the 18.2 write adjustment and 18.1 traversal correction with their owners, and treats child ACL/network confinement, optional CLI config/hook writes, telemetry and native host behavior as unverified qualification gates. Static CodeGraph inspection and the earlier native fixture do not prove those gates. The new finding concerns the exact write authority needed to create `.codegraph` itself before descendant writes; it must be clarified before plan acceptance. Current spec/plan hashes and the seven-file canonical digest match the pinned boundary. Read-only deterministic plan validation returned no errors; it does not assess this authority ambiguity. Invalidated tasks were not used for SpecKit task analysis in plan-only mode.
